continuous_text.title: Our Hometown Workers
continuous_text.content:
Here is Nathaniel. He is a teacher,
He teaches reading at our school.
Here is his friend, Jae, who cooks at Jae's Place.
He makes cooking look so cool.

Here is Maria. She is a doctor.
Each year she checks my eyes and ears.
Now here is Vera. She is a good nurse.
When she gives shots there are no tears.

continuous_text.title: Journal
continuous_text.content:
September 15, 20__
Today was both scary and fun! My mom picked me up early from school. "Come on, Kevin," she said. "We have places to go!"
First, we went to the clinic. I saw my doctor. Her name is Dr. Lopez, and she cares for kids like me. Years ago, her father helped build the clinic! Dr. Lopez said that I am healthy. Yay! No more medicine! I left Dr. Lopez's office with a smile on my face.
Then we went to a new restaurant called Jae's Place. The food was so good! Mom wanted to thank the cook. That's how we met Jae. He is new to our community. Mom told him that soon he will feel like he belongs here.
continuous_text.notes: Kevin's journal entry used for reading strategy modeling.

continuous_text.title: Your Community
continuous_text.content:
What is your community like? Does it have shops? Does it have a park where you can play? Does it have neighbors who say hello? Are there busy streets? Do fire trucks scream as they go by? Or is your community quiet?
Communities are different, but they are also alike in many ways. Communities have people who help take care of you. Firefighters are part of your community. They put out fires. Police officers are also part of your community. They are strong. They protect people. Doctors and nurses in your community help you stay well. They scrub their hands to kill germs. Teachers in your community help you learn. They stress education and exploration.
A community is the place where you live. It is a place where people take care of each other.
continuous_text.notes: Phonics connected text containing target blends (streets, scream, strong, scrub, stress).

continuous_text.title: Li Min's Community
continuous_text.content:
I wake up early.
I say good-bye to Mom and Dad.
They are going to their jobs.
My mom is a nurse, and my dad is a cook.
I don't have school today.
I will spend the day with my grandma in our community.
First we go to our community center.
Grandma meets her friends at the center.
They like to exercise.
Then Grandma and I walk around our community.
We say hello to our friends and neighbors.
We stop at Mr. Wu's food stall.
He gives me a meat sandwich.
Yum!
Mrs. Chen is our neighbor.
She sells vegetables at the market.
Her vegetables are nice and fresh.
We buy some bok choy for dinner.
"Min," I hear someone call.
I look up and see my dad.
"Ba Ba" I say.
Grandma and I stop to eat Dad's dumplings.
My dad is a very good cook.
We walk some more.
We shop some more, and then it is time to go home.
What a great day!
What a great community I live in!
continuous_text.notes: Realistic fiction story by Susan Henderson across pages 13-25.

continuous_text.title: Working Her Way Around the World
continuous_text.content:
Annie Griffiths travels the world and visits many communities. Her job is to take photos of what she sees.

Everybody Works
There are many different jobs in every community. These photos show people at work. Look at all the different jobs people do!
continuous_text.notes: Photo-essay by Claire Cavanaugh; photos by Annie Griffiths (pages 29-31).

continuous_text.title: New in Town
continuous_text.content:
I am new in town. Can you show me around?
Sure, I've lived in this town for three years.
What is this building? A library?
Yes, and this is my school over here!
And where is your home?
Here's my family's home. It is next to the hospital.
Will you be my friend in this great town?
Yes, of course. You can bet I will!

continuous_text.title: The Farmers' Market
continuous_text.content:
Are you looking for a great place to visit? Try the Farmers' Market. It is located at the back of the city park. It is held every Thursday evening.
Farmers come from farms in rural areas about two hours from the city. They pick fresh fruits and vegetables in the morning. Then they drive to our urban park. They set out their food and wait for people to come.
I am there almost every week. It is always crowded. Sometimes it seems like the entire population of our city is out shopping and talking. I don't mind the crowds. I love to buy fresh food, but I love to watch people even more!
continuous_text.notes: Cleo's report used for strategy practice.

continuous_text.title: Using a Community Map
continuous_text.content:
A map shows what is in your community. It can show you where different buildings are. It can help you locate the hospital. It can show you the way to the library.
What can you do for fun? Spread out the map and take a look. Can you see a park where you can play? Can you sprint there? Does your mom drive you there? Is there a zoo you can visit? Maybe you want to find a pool to splash in. Are you hungry? Where can you find a place to get some food?
A community has lots of buildings and fun things to do. A map will help you find them. And when you are ready, a map can show you how to get home.
continuous_text.notes: Phonics connected text containing spl and spr words (spread, sprint, splash).

continuous_text.title: Be My Neighbor
continuous_text.content:
A Special Place
A neighborhood is where you live, learn, play, and work. There are neighborhoods all around the world.
Some neighborhoods have a large population. Others have a very small population. Still, every neighborhood is a special place.
Some neighborhoods are just a few buildings in a village. Others stretch for miles and are part of a big city.
Many neighborhoods have a town square or a plaza in the middle. It is a good place to meet and share news.

A Place to Live
A home can be a place for one family or many families. Home is where people feel safe and comfortable.

A Place to Learn
Neighborhoods have many kinds of schools. Some schools have a lot of rooms. Some have just one room. Some students learn inside a building. Others learn outside.

A Place to Play
In many neighborhoods, you can find a park or a playground. People go there to play.

A Place to Shop
Most neighborhoods have markets, shopping malls, or grocery stores. Families can buy what they need at these places.

A Place to Work
People work together to make a neighborhood a better place. Neighbors might clean up a river or a park. Doctors and firefighters care for people and their safety.

A Place to Celebrate
Special events bring a community together. Parades, parties, and holidays are times for fun and great food.

We Are Neighbors
Neighbors share the place where they live. You are a part of your neighborhood and it's a part of you.

continuous_text.title: My Favorite Place (KidsFavorites Bulletin Board)
continuous_text.content:
Question: What is your favorite place in your community?

Leah (Age: 7, School: Valley View):
My favorite place is the park. There is room to run and play hide-and-seek or baseball. Plus it's a great place to take our dog.

Evan (Age: 7, School: Monte Vista):
I like the library. You can read books on the floor and play on the computers. There's a huge tree outside to climb that you can read under too.

Zoe (Age: 8, School: Seaside Elementary):
My favorite place is the river. We can walk there. I like to see all the bugs and nature there.

Thomas (Age: 8, School: Valley View):
My favorite place is the zoo. I love going there. My favorite things are animals. You can learn a lot about animals there. You should visit the zoo some time.

schema_gaps.observed_content: The 'Big Question' ('What is a community?') acts as an overarching thematic inquiry question driving the entire unit, revisited across openers, reading selections, synthesis graphic organizers, and wrap-up projects.
schema_gaps.problem: The schema does not provide a dedicated entity or field for guiding unit inquiry questions, forcing it to be split between unit metadata notes and language records.
schema_gaps.proposed_change: Add an optional 'inquiry_questions' or 'big_question' field to the Unit object, or create an inquiry_focus curriculum component.
schema_gaps.reason: Tracking Big Questions across units and series is critical for thematic and cross-curricular mapping.

schema_gaps.observed_content: In-text active reading prompts ('Before You Continue', 'Preview', 'Predict') embedded throughout continuous reading texts at specific paragraph/page intervals.
schema_gaps.problem: Treating intermittent reading margin prompts as standalone activity records dissociates them from their exact position inside the continuous text flow.
schema_gaps.proposed_change: Introduce an embedded 'intermittent_prompts' or 'checkpoints' array within continuous_text records, or add an anchor/page offset field.
schema_gaps.reason: Allows precise reconstruction of guided reading interactions as students read page by page.

schema_gaps.observed_content: Running page-foot vocabulary glosses providing simplified definitions for low-frequency words encountered in texts (e.g., 'exercise: do physical activity', 'food stall: a place where you can buy snacks and sweets').
schema_gaps.problem: Current vocabulary record structure does not capture student-facing glossary definitions provided directly on the page.
schema_gaps.proposed_change: Add a 'student_definition' or 'source_gloss' string field to the vocabulary record schema.
schema_gaps.reason: Preserves the textbook publisher's pedagogical scaffolding definitions for readability analysis.
